blueprint_topic: Management of Care — ethical nursing advocacy and active collaboration during resuscitation-preference and surrogate decision discussions
stem: A family is participating in a goals-of-care discussion about resuscitation for a client who cannot currently make decisions. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Clarify information within nursing scope, support the surrogate's questions, advocate for the client's known values, and collaborate with the health care team.
options.B: Present the available code-status options and ask the surrogate to choose before further team discussion, to reduce conflicting messages from different clinicians.
options.C: Have the primary provider conduct the resuscitation discussion, then reinforce the decision after the order is entered so nursing does not influence the preference.
options.D: Explain the nurse's view of likely burdens and benefits and recommend the code status the nurse believes is best, while leaving the final choice to the surrogate.

rationale: A is correct. The current ANA position statement on end-of-life care states that nurses should collaborate with other members of the health care team, support patients and families, and participate in decision-making processes that reflect physiologic realities and patient preferences. ANA's DNR position statement further states that nurses advocate for and play an active role in resuscitation discussions, assist patients, families and surrogate decision-makers in making informed choices, provide accurate and understandable information, foster interdisciplinary discussion, and ensure that patient wishes are respected. B is incorrect because asking the surrogate to choose before appropriate interdisciplinary discussion undermines the informed collaborative process. C is incorrect because ANA explicitly describes an active nursing role rather than complete withdrawal from the discussion. D is incorrect because the nurse should support informed, preference-centered decision-making rather than steer the surrogate toward the nurse's personal code-status preference.
educational_objective: Actively support informed resuscitation decisions by clarifying information within scope, supporting surrogate questions, advocating for the client's known values, and collaborating with the interdisciplinary team without coercing or substituting the nurse's own decision.
source_organization: American Nurses Association (ANA); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Nurses' Roles and Responsibilities in Providing Care and Support at the End of Life; Nursing Care and Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) Decisions; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: ANA end-of-life position statement effective/approved 2024 and current on ANA official position-statement index when rechecked 2026-08-20; ANA DNR revised position statement effective 2020 and current on ANA/OJIN resources; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: ANA 2024 end-of-life position statement, Statement of ANA Position: nurses collaborate with the health care team, support the patient/family, and participate in decision-making processes reflecting physiologic realities and patient preferences; goals-of-care discussion may involve palliative care, ethics, and legal/risk management. ANA DNR position statement, Purpose/Statement/Recommendations: nurse's role includes assisting patients, families, surrogate decision-makers and team members in informed DNR choices; nurses advocate for and play an active role in resuscitation discussions; provide accurate, complete and understandable information; support weighing benefits/burdens/risks; advocate for interdisciplinary collaboration and ensure patient wishes are respected. Current ANA position-statement index lists the end-of-life statement under 2024 Ethics and Human Rights. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care supports advocacy, client rights/preferences, advance directives, ethical practice, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
source_claim_supported: Current ANA guidance directly supports an active but noncoercive nursing role in resuscitation/goals-of-care discussions: collaboration, information clarification within scope, surrogate support, and advocacy for patient values without substituting the nurse's preference or decision. NCSBN supports the ethical advocacy and Management of Care construct.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: protect client rights and autonomy, integrate advance directives/preferences, advocate for the client, follow legal/ethical requirements, and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members.

ANA clinical/ethical evidence used for Q1976 is current HTML. ANA PDF search results were not relied on as visual evidence, so no new ANA PDF visual verification is claimed.
correction_summary: Original Q1976 had a 177-character correct answer versus much shorter distractors and an absolute-word distractor. The item was rebuilt so all four options are plausible nursing roles in a resuscitation discussion and are closely balanced in length. The key now requires active collaborative advocacy without making the final surrogate decision or steering the family toward the nurse's personal preference.

option_audit.A: Correct; matches ANA's active nursing role in clarification, surrogate support, patient-preference advocacy, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
option_audit.B: Plausible efficiency-focused shortcut; incorrect because informed resuscitation decision-making should not bypass appropriate team discussion before the surrogate chooses.
option_audit.C: Plausible scope-protection overcorrection; incorrect because ANA explicitly expects nurses to participate actively rather than wait until after an order is entered.
option_audit.D: Plausible counseling overreach; incorrect because the nurse should clarify and support informed decisions without steering the surrogate toward the nurse's personally preferred code status.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on all/only/always/never/must/entirely-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 159, B 163, C 164, D 162 characters; the correct answer is the shortest by a small margin and there is no length cue.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives describe credible nursing communication roles and differ in collaboration, timing, or coercion rather than obvious tone.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. B prematurely truncates collaborative discussion, C removes the nurse from a role ANA explicitly assigns, and D introduces nurse-directed preference steering. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
